rounds.text: NDA Securities Ltd is backed by a robust financial sector tailwind with a tailwind score of +0.78 [E63], alongside strong recent top-line momentum featuring a 107% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E17] and a quarterly operating margin reaching 43% in September 2026 compared to -77% in the year-ago quarter [E28]. The balance sheet remains a distinct asset, featuring near-debt-free status with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.05x [E34, E46], comfortable short-term liquidity supported by a current ratio of 2.34x [E35], and positive operational generation yielding Rs 1.81 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 1.02 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026 [E32, E33]. Furthermore, internal confidence is visibly climbing as promoters have steadily increased their holding from 48.57% in December 2023 to 58.82% by September 2026 [E38], while capital efficiency metrics like ROCE at 9.55% outperform the sector benchmark of 5.88% [E10]. Operational improvements are further evidenced by a dramatic drop in debtor days from 122 to 83.5 and working capital requirements shrinking from 138 to 67.5 days [E48, E49]. Conceded: [E13, E18, E40, E60].

The current valuation of NDA Securities Ltd is fundamentally disconnected from its underlying financial performance, as evidenced by a steep P/E ratio of 45.3x [E1]. While the company has seen recent volatility in operating margins [E29, E30], the long-term reality is a history of poor capital efficiency, characterized by a median return on equity of only 3% over the last decade [E23] and a current ROE of -0.7% [E13]. Investors are paying a premium for a business that has failed to deliver consistent value, with the share price declining 38% over the last year [E22] and a DCF analysis suggesting the stock is significantly overvalued by 94.3% [E41]. Furthermore, the company’s earnings are propped up by non-core items, specifically Rs 0.48 Cr in other income [E51], and the market is currently pricing in an aggressive 19.4% earnings growth rate that far exceeds the base case assumption of 10% [E42]. Conceded: the company maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.05x [E34] and has shown a significant 107% growth in compounded sales over the trailing twelve months [E17]. Despite these isolated improvements, the persistent inconsistency in profit growth, which sits at -63% for the trailing twelve months [E18], suggests that the market's optimism is not supported by the company's historical ability to generate sustainable returns.

The bear’s focus on the P/E ratio [E1] ignores the company's massive operational transformation, where quarterly operating margins surged by 120 percentage points year-over-year [E28]. While the bear cites historical ROE [E23], it fails to account for the company's aggressive recent sales growth of 107% [E17] and 17% over three years [E16], which signals a fundamental shift in scale rather than a stagnant past. Conceded: the trailing twelve-month profit growth is -63% [E18] and the DCF model suggests overvaluation [E41]. However, the bear overlooks that the company is now almost debt-free [E46] with a strong current ratio of 2.34x [E35], providing the financial stability to support this growth. Furthermore, the bear’s reliance on other income [E51] ignores the tangible improvement in efficiency, specifically the reduction in debtor days from 122 to 83.5 [E48] and working capital requirements from 138 to 67.5 days [E49]. Finally, the bear ignores that promoter confidence is at an all-time high, with holdings increasing by 10.25 percentage points since 2023 [E38], suggesting that those closest to the business see value that the stale DCF model misses [E62].

The bull’s reliance on a single quarter of margin expansion [E28] ignores that the yearly operating-margin trend remains inconsistent [E29], and the long-term trend shows a 10-percentage-point decline over three years [E27]. While the bull highlights recent sales growth [E17], it fails to reconcile this with the reality that compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months is -63% [E18]. Conceded: the company is nearly debt-free [E46] and has improved working capital efficiency [E48, E49]. However, this operational improvement has not translated into shareholder returns, as evidenced by a -38% share price growth over the last year [E22] and a median return on equity that has languished at 3% over the last decade [E23]. The bull’s dismissal of the DCF model [E40, E41] is dangerous, as the current market price already demands an aggressive 19.4% earnings growth rate to justify its valuation [E42]. Finally, while promoter holdings have increased [E38], this does not negate the fact that the company’s actual return on equity is currently negative at -0.7% [E13, E26].
